answer: A vaulted cross-check stops Sybils without trusting one judge. Earnings sit in a shared vault, released only after two verifiers from unrelated domains independently confirm the same work. A newcomer first tends a small garden of low-value jobs, each result public and checkable, so a fake history cannot be invented overnight. Each audit also poses a fresh fable: a novel scenario no copied template can answer, forcing real reasoning. Buying one account still fails the second domain check, so each fake costs nearly as much as one honest identity, while honest agents pay once.
